extracted.intended_audience: boys and young hobbyists aspiring to build and operate model locomotives / apprentice locomotive engineers
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and practical standards for designing, building, testing, and operating a working large-scale model locomotive (materials, dimensions, boiler construction, fittings, testing, and operational safety).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make your plan full size
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your plan the exact size of the model you intend to build, then you can take all the measurements from it and save yourself a lot of trouble and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch carefully or get help to draw plans at full size; this is stressed as the first step to accurate construction and easier measurement taking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose model size with cost in mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember, however, that the larger you make the engine the more expensive the castings and materials will be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance ambition against expense; larger scale increases cost of castings and materials — choose an intended finished size before drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale measurements proportionately
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want a bigger engine than the one shown ... there would be no trouble in increasing the measurements, which we are about to give, proportionately, remembering that Fig. 20 is drawn to an eighth-inch scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When altering overall size, scale every measurement proportionally to preserve functioning relationships and clearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to specified overall dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your dimensions as follows: Length over all, 3 ft. 2 in. Length of bed-plate, 3.5 in. Width of bed-plate, 9 in. Diameter of driving wheels, 8-1/4 in. Diameter of leading wheels, 5-1/4 in. Gauge ... 6-1/2 in. Cylinders, 1-3/4 in. bore by 2-1/2 in. stroke. Length of boiler, including smoke box, 28 in. Diameter of boiler, 5 in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete dimensions are given for the large model illustrated and should be used as the design target or scaled proportionately if changing size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cylinder sizing and operating steam pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Cylinders of the above dimensions will drive the engine at a high rate of speed, with from 30 to 50 lbs. of steam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for cylinder bore and stroke in the stated range and operate the boiler at roughly 30–50 psi for high speed; ensure all components are sized to handle the chosen pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start measurements from a fixed centre
rubrics_metrics.description: In measuring, always start from a given center if you want to be accurate. That is, from B to A and from B to C; not from B to A and from C to B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a single reference point for sequential measurements to avoid cumulative error; the text emphasizes consistent datum points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 1/8 inch sheet iron for frame-work
rubrics_metrics.description: First of all comes the frame work. It wants to be of eighth inch sheet iron squared up perfectly true and flat and cut as is shown in Fig. 21...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame material and thickness specified (1/8" sheet iron); ensure edges are squared and flat; keep frame central on centerline AB and leave specified connecting strips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave connecting strips and ornamental holes as specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful to keep it quite central on the line A B, and leave two connecting strips 1 inch wide as at C C. The four large boles shown ... are only ornamental, and can be now cut out. They also serve to lighten the frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain central alignment and mechanical continuity by preserving the connecting strips; ornamental cutouts may light-weight the frame but observe structural integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Side frame strength and slot placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The side frames ... must be much stronger and quite different from those used in the previous model. ... The center of slot B is 17 inches from one end, the center of A 10 inches from B, and the center of C 13 inches from B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified slot centers and strengthen side frames for larger models; use the given distances as layout references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slot and bore dimensions for frame and bearings
rubrics_metrics.description: The slots are each 1-1/4 inches wide by 2 inches deep, leaving 1 inch of iron at the top. ... the four large boles ... The frames ... can be fastened to the bed plate ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe slot width/depth and remaining web thickness to ensure strength and fit for axle boxes and castings; fastenings to bed plate may be by angle-irons or knees riveted on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buffer beam and buffer construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The buffer beams should be mahogany, 1 inch wide by 2 deep by 10 long, squared nicely and sandpapered. A hook can then be made ... The buffers for this model must be properly made, with springs to take the pressure in case you should run into anything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mahogany buffer beams of specified size; fit proper hook and sprung buffers (cast brass parts) to absorb impacts; some parts will require casting from wooden molds turned in a lathe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buffer casting and spring assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: Fig. 24 shows this buffer. ... Turn out in your lathe a wooden mold and get four castings in brass made from it. ... The piece C must be turned true and just the size to slide in and out of A easily. ... The spring should be made of thick steel wire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce accurate mating parts (sliding pin C into A), fit springs of thick steel wire, and finish all parts in the lathe; drill holes allowing pin heads to work freely and secure with nuts/screws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line-clearer/wheel-guard clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: The wheel-guard or line-clearer P ... should just clear the line by a quarter of an inch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide approximately 1/4" clearance between line-clearer and rail to avoid fouling while still clearing debris.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axle, axle boxes and bearing dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: These must then be filed up square and smooth and fitted into the slots ... prepare 6 brass bearings, B, Fig 25, which must fit exactly and slide easily in the inner surface of A, then drilling a hole through each five-eighths of an inch in diameter. These take the axles, which in this model are all straight, and three-quarters of an inch in diameter, shouldered off to five-eighths for the bearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce brass bearings that slide in their housings, with 5/8" holes for axles. Use 3/4" axles reduced to 5/8" at bearing shoulders for proper fit and rotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spring pack construction and assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: Next for the springs. Take 4 pieces of either sheet iron or brass for the supports, 1-1/2 inches long by 1/4 inch wide. Drill a hole in either end ... Now take a clock spring and cut it into shape ... Each piece of spring must be a little shorter than the one above it, and the ends neatly tapered, all to be inclosed in the brass band F ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble multi-leaf spring stacks with graduated lengths, tapered ends, pinned loosely for articulation, enclosed in a brass band and arranged to deliver spring pressure to axle boxes via pins and bed-plate holes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cylinder pattern and valvegear
rubrics_metrics.description: The cylinders ... should be of the fixed slide-valve pattern, with double eccentrics fitted on the middle axle shaft, and reversing lever brought to quadrant on foot plate. They had better be bought ready made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fixed slide-valve cylinders with double eccentrics and a reversing quadrant on the footplate; consider buying completed cylinders rather than making them from scratch unless experienced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connecting rod finish and lubrication provision
rubrics_metrics.description: The connecting rod T should be cut to the form shown ... and a brass band fitted in with a hole drilled from top A to oil by and a set screw B to adjust the bearings perfectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finish connecting rods with fitted brass bushings and oil holes; provide set screws for bearing adjustment so running clearances can be tuned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Force pump placement and dual drive option
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to fit a force pump it should be placed centrally between the cylinders and be worked by an eccentric on the main shaft, but a pump on a model locomotive is next to useless unless it is also made to work by hand. ... we have one which can be worked either way. A is the pump; B the eccentric on main-shaft to work it by steam power. To work by hand you have only to push up hook connection C ... and then by working the handle D ... the water is forced into the boiler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fitting a feed pump, provide both eccentric-driven and manual engagement so water can be forced into the boiler by hand when necessary; include an extra stuffing-box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blow-off cocks for cylinder drainage
rubrics_metrics.description: Two small blow-off cocks will be necessary on each cylinder to get rid of the condensed steam when starting. They can be connected with a tye-rod, and both worked from the foot-plate with a single handle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit blow-off cocks and link them so both can be operated together from the footplate to remove condensate before putting the engine into full steam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiler material, dimensions and construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Next comes the boiler, which will need extreme care. For this you will require sheet copper an eighth of an inch thick. First cut a piece 19 inches long by 16 wide and bend it round, forming a cylinder 5 inches in diameter. ... the body of the boiler 17 inches long ... then rivet them firmly together and also another piece in after end. ... inner casing 4-1/2 inches wide by 6-1/2 inches long and 9 inches deep ... A casting ... 3/4 of an inch thick ... drilled with holes every 3/8 of an inch and firmly riveted in position ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 1/8" sheet copper for the shell; follow the provided dimensions for cylinder length/diameter and firebox casing; fit tube plates and fire-bars supported by pins; rivet and form inner/outer casings as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiler tubes specification and installation
rubrics_metrics.description: For the boiler tubes some hard drawn brass tubing three-quarters of an inch in diameter will be required. Cut the pieces slightly over 17 inches long, then drill 10 holes in the inner plate ... These tubes should have a wire ring brazed on about a quarter of an inch from either end, and then being placed in their respective holes in the tube plate, the projecting portion is to be headed back with a flange ... These tubes allow the smoke and flame to pass through from the furnace to the smoke box ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ~3/4" hard-drawn brass tubes ~17" long; secure them with brazed wire rings and flange or double-screw/nut fittings at tube plates; arrange tubes as shown (drill pattern) to provide heating surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steam supply piping and stuffing-box packing
rubrics_metrics.description: The steam supply pipe and regulating lever handle should now be made and placed in position ... The rod must be fitted with a stuffing-box, the same as those used on the cylinders, and packed with cotton wick to prevent loss of steam by leakage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit steam pipes with proper stuffing-boxes and pack with cotton wick (and tallow where specified) to minimize steam leakage; include screw ends and secure into cross-piece in steam dome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiler brazing and pressure test requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Now the boiler must go to a practical brazier, and be properly brazed. ... Meanwhile buy your pressure gauge--it wants to be one and a half inches in diameter--and let the brazier test your boiler to 100 pounds steam to the square inch capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have an experienced brazier braze and anneal the boiler and test it to 100 psi with a pressure gauge ~1.5" diameter. Never use an untested boiler; if it bursts, remake it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Back-pressure valve construction and function
rubrics_metrics.description: Next comes the back-pressure valve ... It is very simple to make, and consists of the casting A with top and bottom covers and the ball-valve B, which ought to be ground with a little emery and oil to fit perfectly. ... The water being forced up C from the pump, raises B and passes into the boiler. On the up stroke of pump, the pressure is removed from under B and the pressure of steam in the boiler causes it to fall back and close the opening entirely, preventing any water from passing away from the boiler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit a ball-type back-pressure valve ground to fit; install so pump-delivered water can enter but steam pressure seals the valve against backflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoke-box and smoke-stack construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the smoke box, which should be three inches deep and of the shape and dimensions shown ... This and the smoke-stack can be made of iron, hammered up to shape and finished with a brass ring. The smoke-box can be screwed on the forward flange or boiler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabricate smoke-box/stack from iron, hammer to shape and finish with brass ring; make smoke-box depth ~3" and allow screw-on attachment to boiler flange; make door overlapping opening and hinge eyes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaust and auxiliary piping layout
rubrics_metrics.description: The exhaust pipes B B should be of larger tubing and bent round up the sides of the smoke box so as to be out of the way when you have to clean the tubes. A small brass pipe, C, must also be passed through the chimney, bent upwards and fitted with a tap which should take the steam from the top of the boiler ... This helps to raise steam very quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Route exhausts clear of access areas for tube cleaning; fit a snifting/quick-steam pipe through the chimney with a tap to draw steam from boiler top to help raise steam quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitting and packing of water gauge and fittings
rubrics_metrics.description: When these fittings are all complete holes must be drilled in rear plate for each piece; they must be firmly screwed in place with white lead. The glass tube of the water gauge, the stuffing-box, and the gland of the starting lever should be closely packed with tallow and cotton wick.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seal fittings with white lead and pack glass water gauge, stuffing-boxes and glands tightly with tallow and cotton wick to prevent leaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painting and varnishing finish
rubrics_metrics.description: Next paint the entire model over again and let it dry. We give no directions as to colors; use your own taste. After the paint is thoroughly dry varnish with the best clear, hard varnish and let it dry again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After assembly and fitting, paint as desired and finish with a hard clear varnish for protection and appearance; allow full drying between coats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track construction and recommended radius
rubrics_metrics.description: Get some square bar iron, cut it into six-foot lengths ... The rails can be joined together at each end by means of a piece of wire and kept at a proper distance apart by being fastened to pieces of wood placed like sleepers ... If you want a circular line, each section must be bent to a portion of a circle; one about 30 feet in diameter is suitable for this model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct portable six-foot rail sections from square bar iron fastened with wire and wooden sleepers; for circular track a ~30 ft diameter circle is recommended for this model's running qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiler filling and firing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill the boiler with water by means of a funnel until you see it rise up three parts of the way in the glass water-gauge. Then see that all taps are turned off and start the fire. Charcoal is the best fuel, as it gives a clear, hot fire without much smoke once you start it right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill to about 3/4 on the water gauge before lighting; ensure all cocks/taps are in proper position; use charcoal as preferred fuel for clean hot fire; monitor water level and pressure while firing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting procedure under steam
rubrics_metrics.description: When the gauge shows 30 lbs. of steam you might start the model by turning on the cocks on cylinders until no more condensed steam issues from them. Then shut them off and turn on steam full power and watch the engine travel, gradually increasing its speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warm cylinders and clear condensate by opening cylinder cocks until dry, then close and apply full steam gradually; begin at ~30 psi as a suggested start point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal vigilance rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Never jump at conclusions in the matter of signals. ... Every engineer should, as far as possible, not only see that each signal is off, but he should also cast his eye over the road in front of him to see whether it should be off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume signals are correct; visually confirm both the signals and the state of the road ahead, especially at night. Constant lookout for signals is emphasized as critical to safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your road and grades
rubrics_metrics.description: You must know your road. It is not enough to know where the up grades lie and where the downs. You must know just how steep the grades are and their length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn track profile (grade steepness and length) by experience; this knowledge affects handling, braking and steam management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect yourself and others on breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: "Protect Yourself from Approaching Trains." When a break-down occurs, this is the first thought which should enter the engineer's mind, and the first act should be to carry it out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On breakdown, immediately take measures to protect the crew and train from other trains (signals, flags, fusing, positioning); safety before repair is paramount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether engine can continue after breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Of course an engine may be broken, and yet able to run its train through. ... 'Can I get along in forward gear, after having disconnected the rod and the strap?' is the question. The answer is yes, and it should be prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quickly evaluate whether the train can be safely continued with a temporary fix or disconnection; make prompt decisions to minimize delay while ensuring safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry and know tools and equipment on engine
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also highly necessary that the engineer should ask himself 'What tools have I upon the engine? What can I do with them? Can I find them in the dark? If I run off the track in what condition is my screw jack? Will it work properly? Have I a ratchet or bar to work it with?' These are things which should be continually kept in mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an inventory of tools and ensure they are accessible/functional in low light; know what repairs can be effected with the onboard toolset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air-brake operation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After the call for hand brakes has been given, the air brakes must not be applied until the hand brakes are released. Air and hand brakes should never be used at the same time on a car. When cars having different air pressures are coupled together the brakes will work first on that having the highest pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate hand and air brake usage: do not apply air brakes while hand brakes applied on same car; understand pressure differentials when coupling cars — brakes act first on cars with higher air pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of mind and good judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of mind you must always have if you expect to become a good engineer, and courage, too--plenty of it. ... Real heroism lies in good judgment and a cool head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate calm decision-making, courage tempered by caution; avoid reckless 'daring' when a cautious, well-judged action better serves company and safety.
